items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1976-02-13
items.q: There was Bix standing out there, you know. Bix and Trombau. Paul Merez from the Rhythm Kings, you know. ... We walked right into the conversation, you know.

ctx.x: And it wasn't his style. And you know, this, I think, really did something to Sharky because he never would say very much if you mentioned Bix around him. And I can understand it, you know, I mean, it kind of gave him a terrible complex, I guess. But really, he wasn't deserving of this because it was a mistake. I think it was Paul Merez or someone who thought that Sharky could fill that bill, you see. Oh, I see. But Sharky's style, as Dick Allen says, anyone who knew Sharky would just know that Sharky was not the…
What, as close as you can figure out, what was the style of that Wolverines group? Was it, did they connect it all with any more?

items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1960-07-14
items.q: Of course, I met him out at Paul Merez's house when Vic was in town with Paul Whiteman.

ctx.x: And, of course, I can't forget Vic's Beiderback, the time that he taught me in the middle of the and he taught me in a mist. I can't forget that. That was a lesson that was really a great lesson. Of course, I met him out at Paul Merez's house when Vic was in town with Paul Whiteman. And I would say that covering piano teachers would go back to listening to different piano players. You listen and you learn. And I think that's the way most of the old timers did. They listened and they learned. And one thing about…
Kind of like a Wausau just played for fun. They just go around and listen and pick up things. That's right.
